name: HTRA1-related Autosomal Dominant Cerebral Small Vessel Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for HTRA1-related Autosomal Dominant CSVD

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic heterozygous mutation in the HTRA1 gene
Presence of progressive subcortical ischemic events including lacunar strokes and cognitive decline
Brain MRI showing extensive white matter hyperintensities predominantly in periventricular and deep white matter regions
Autosomal dominant family history of cerebral small vessel disease or stroke
Exclusion of other causes of cerebral small vessel disease such as CADASIL or sporadic small vessel disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Pathogenic HTRA1 mutation plus clinical features of subcortical ischemic events and characteristic MRI findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; clinical and imaging features support diagnosis.

searchTerms: gradual thinking decline from small vessel disease
progressive cognitive problems due to brain vessels

pathognomonic.symptomName: Extensive confluent white matter hyperintensities on MRI
pathognomonic.notes: Radiological hallmark rather than clinical symptom
searchTerms: large areas of white matter damage on brain scan
extensive brain white spots on MRI
widespread brain tissue changes on imaging

common.symptomName: Gait disturbance due to subcortical ischemic damage
searchTerms: walking problems from small brain strokes
gait issues due to brain blood flow damage
seizures caused by brain blood flow loss

rare.symptomName: Visual field defects due to subcortical infarcts
searchTerms: partial loss of side vision from brain injury
blind spots due to small brain strokes
visual field loss from brain infarcts

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific biomarkers identified
imaging: MRI brain showing extensive confluent white matter hyperintensities on T2/FLAIR sequences
Lacunar infarcts predominantly in basal ganglia, thalamus, and pons
Absence of cerebral microbleeds typical of other small vessel diseases
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of granular osmiophilic material on skin biopsy
Characteristic anterior temporal lobe white matter lesions on MRI
HTRA1 homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations
Association with vascular risk factors such as hypertension and diabetes

redFlags: Early-onset recurrent lacunar strokes without vascular risk factors
Family history of autosomal dominant stroke or dementia
Rapid progression of cognitive decline with extensive white matter changes on MRI
